reports.title: DICK'S Sporting Goods, Inc. Reports Third Quarter Results

guidance.heading: Full Year 2026 Outlook
section: The Company's Full Year Outlook for 2026 is presented below.

desk.headline: Sales up 23.2% to $5.13bn and adjusted EPS of $1.94, both above estimates; full-year EPS outlook raised
results: Sales rose 23.2% to $5.13bn, mainly because Foot Locker was owned for the whole quarter this year versus about eight weeks last year; this beat the $5.08bn estimate.
Adjusted EPS fell 6% to $1.94 but was well above the $1.41 estimate; GAAP EPS more than doubled to $1.87 as last year's deal costs fell away.
The core DICK'S business grew comparable sales 2.6% with segment profit of $290.6m, roughly flat on last year.
Foot Locker returned to slightly positive comparable sales (+0.5%), led by the US Foot Locker banner (over 4%), and trimmed its loss to $40.9m.
DICK'S bought back 6.7m shares for $903m in the quarter, funded partly by $1bn of new bonds; cash fell to $464m and inventory rose 9%.

guidance.summary: Full-year EPS guidance raised to $11.45–12.30 adjusted (from $11.00–12.00); the midpoint sits above the $11.51 consensus. Sales outlook of $22.0–22.2bn is in line with expectations. Higher DICK'S Business profit outlook; Foot Locker outlook unchanged.

points: Management said the DICK'S business is gaining market share, helped by a strong back-to-school season; growth came from a higher average ticket while transactions dipped.
CEO Lauren Hobart said all income groups grew and she saw no sign of shoppers trading down.
Ed Stack said there is too much old product in the sneaker channel, keeping the market promotional possibly into 2027; Nike's Jordan reset is weighing mostly on Foot Locker.
Foot Locker's turnaround was described as a long process, with more store closures under review and Europe expected to take longer than North America.
A warm October hurt cold-weather categories; a 2027 outlook will come with Q4 results, with SG&A growth expected to slow.
call.source: Call coverage: The Motley Fool transcript, 24 Nov 2026; Seeking Alpha via TradingView, 24 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Foot Locker's small comp gain holds once it joins the comparable-sales base in Q4.
Holiday promotions and sneaker-market clearance, which management expects to last into 2027.
Inventory (up 9%, Foot Locker up 16%) and the rest of the up-to-$750m Foot Locker clean-up charges.
